reason: Avoid abstractions without a consumer need
exceptions: Existing abstractions or actual substitution needs can justify interfaces and generics
A zero value may be unusable when validation or dependencies are essential

reason: Use encapsulation where invariants need it
exceptions: Exported record and serialization fields can be appropriate
Clear bools and established signatures may remain

reason: Return expected failures without losing the result
exceptions: Panics can represent programming defects; some concrete operations cannot fail

reason: Retain semantic error information promised to callers
exceptions: Hiding a lower-level cause can be an intentional API boundary

reason: Release owned resources on all relevant paths
exceptions: Do not close caller-owned resources without an ownership contract

reason: Make cancellation reach the actual request-scoped work
exceptions: Independent background work needs an explicitly owned separate lifetime

reason: Give background work termination and completion ownership
exceptions: Long-lived work is valid when an application owns and joins it

reason: Prevent unsafe sharing and copying synchronization state
exceptions: A passing race run only covers executed behavior

reason: Preserve observable absence, ordering, and aliasing
exceptions: A requested semantic change can deliberately revise the contract

reason: Validate numeric bounds required by the contract
exceptions: Not all arithmetic needs overflow checking; ordinary counters may have sufficient bounds

reason: Verify observable success and failure behavior
exceptions: Table tests and a particular assertion framework are choices, not universal requirements

reason: Keep changed public contracts discoverable to callers
exceptions: Document affected APIs and non-obvious behavior; avoid unrelated boilerplate cleanup
